introH2: 🏝️ Doing Koh Larn on a budget — how to pick a value stay that fits your trip?
introHtml: Koh Larn is known for resorts and pool villas that run into the thousands of baht a night, but the truth is there are more value and budget stays tucked around the island than most people expect — and that's what makes doing Koh Larn on a budget more fun than it sounds. Some are small seaside places a few minutes' walk from the Na Ban pier; some are clean village guesthouses that cost a fraction of the beachfront rate; some are resorts right on Tawaen and Samae Beach where you can walk down to the sand, for low four figures. Many travellers pay top rates for a beachfront room they only use to sleep — money that could go on seafood and boat trips instead. This guide brings together 10 value and budget Koh Larn stays we've reviewed in depth, ranked by value, across the Na Ban pier area, Tawaen Beach and Samae Beach — every pick comes from reading real guest reviews, with honest pros and cons, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Koh Larn has no city-style public transport. Getting to the island means a ferry from Bali Hai pier in Pattaya to Na Ban pier or Tawaen pier (the regular ferry takes about 45 minutes; speedboats are faster but pricier). On the island you get around by shared songthaew, by renting a scooter (around ฿300/day), or with your hotel's shuttle. The value areas in this guide: Na Ban village / pier — near the pier, shops and market, walk to your room off the boat; most budget stays are here (Toonja, Kampu, Lareena, Suntosa, White House, Sea Side, Rimtalay) · Tawaen Beach — the lively main beach, walk down to the water (Tawaen; The Castello is near the beach with a free shuttle) · Samae Beach — quieter beach with lovely water, walk from your room to the sand (Xanadu). Bring cash — many shops and stays on the island prefer it over cards, and because everything is shipped over by boat, prices on the island run a little higher than in Pattaya.

entries.storyHtml: In this guide, Toonja is the best-value pick — 9.2 from 72 reviews on Trip.com, at a starting price of just ฿1,100. It's a small seaside Bed & Breakfast that sits about a 3-minute walk from the Na Ban pier, with a free golf-cart pickup from the pier and free breakfast, so you get off the boat and reach your room fast without a songthaew across the island. It takes adults 18+ only, so it stays quiet and suits couples and travellers after a proper rest, and there's a King room with a sea view. Honest notes from the reviews: it's a small B&B with no pool, compact rooms, a fairly basic breakfast, and no children. If you're judging on location, cleanliness and price, Toonja is one of the best-value beds on the island.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, take the King Room with Sea View to wake up to the water; and since it's adults-only, families with kids should pick elsewhere on this list. Message ahead to confirm the golf-cart pickup time so you don't have to drag bags from the pier.

entries.storyHtml: Kampu is a small boutique resort in Na Ban village that wins on extras — 9.0 from 53 reviews, from ฿1,600 with breakfast included, a free pier shuttle, and a free scooter to ride around on, which cuts a big chunk out of your on-island transport. It suits travellers doing Koh Larn on a budget who spend the day out at the beaches and come back just to sleep, for far less than a beachfront room. Rooms are simple but clean, with cold air-con and hot water. Honest notes from the reviews: it's not on the sea and has no pool, so you ride the scooter to Tawaen and Samae Beach yourself, and it's a small resort with simple facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Confirm the free scooter and pier shuttle with the property when you book — that's where the real savings are. There's no beach or pool here, so use the free scooter to reach Tawaen and Samae Beach easily.

entries.storyHtml: The Castello is a Tuscan-castle-themed boutique resort that brings a lot of character on a light budget — 8.8 from 104 reviews, from ฿1,200. What guests mention most is how photogenic every corner is, with arches and Italian-style stucco walls, an in-house cafe and fresh bakery, and a free shuttle between the Na Ban pier and Tawaen Beach so you're not hauling bags far. It suits travellers who want a stay with style and photos at an affordable island price. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool, so you head to the beach to swim, and the cheapest (Large Economy) rooms are fairly compact.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Standard Room with a balcony over the cheapest Large Economy for a brighter feel. There's no pool, so use the free shuttle to swim at Tawaen Beach, then come back to photograph the resort and hit the in-house cafe and bakery.

entries.storyHtml: Xanadu is the best-value beachfront pick — 8.9, and the most-reviewed stay in this guide at over 754 reviews, from just ฿1,900. What guests mention most is the location right on Samae Beach, which is quieter than Tawaen, with clear water, a free private beach with loungers and breakfast by the sea, and you can walk straight from your room down to the sand. It's a roughly 68-room resort that suits anyone who wants to sleep by the water without paying villa rates. Honest notes from the reviews: the in-room water is filtered seawater and some amenities aren't complete, the building is starting to show its age, and the island is quiet at night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a sea-view room when you book — some look straight onto Samae Beach — and since the in-room water is filtered seawater, keep some drinking water for brushing your teeth.

entries.storyHtml: Lareena is a boutique resort right by the Na Ban pier with the most reviews in this tier — 548 — scoring 9.0, from ฿2,450. What guests mention most is that you step off the boat and walk straight to your room, walk to the shops and market in the community, and there are sea-facing rooms with balconies at a fair price for the location. It's the pick if your budget stretches a little further and you weight convenience by the pier and a well-reviewed track record first, with no long walk from the boat. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool, some rooms have older furniture, and being right by the pier means you'll hear boat horns and pier noise at times.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, step up to a Superior Sea Side or Suite On Sea for a sea-facing room with a balcony — better value than garden view. There's no pool here, so if a pool is a must, choose elsewhere on the list.

entries.storyHtml: Rimtalay is a small white-and-blue-themed resort where every room sees the sea — 8.6 from 132 reviews, from ฿1,800. What guests mention most is the Santorini-style photo spots, the rooftop pool and sea-view jacuzzi, breakfast included, and a private fishing jetty. Getting a sea-view room with a pool for high-four-figures is good value, and it's quiet and couple-friendly. It suits travellers here to relax and take photos more than to swim hard, since the resort's frontage isn't a sandy beach you walk straight into. Honest note: there are quirks around water pressure and bathroom lighting worth asking about before you book.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for an upper-floor Sea View Room for a more open view. The frontage isn't a sandy beach, so to swim you take a songthaew/scooter to Tawaen or Samae Beach — and ask about water pressure before booking.

entries.storyHtml: Tawaen Beach Resort sits on Tawaen Beach, the main and liveliest beach on Koh Larn — 8.5 from 212 reviews, from ฿1,800. It's only about 150 metres to the sea, an easy walk down to swim, with free beach chairs, a seaside restaurant, snorkelling and squid-fishing trips, and a songthaew pickup from the pier. There are several room types from couples up to bigger families, so it suits anyone who wants to sleep by the island's most popular beach at an accessible price. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool, the thin sliding doors let some noise through from neighbours, breakfast is on the small side, and service can be inconsistent at times.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Tawaen is busy and crowded midday, so swim early if you want it quieter. If your budget allows, the Triple/Quadruple rooms are better value for a group, and check the songthaew pickup times from the pier with the property first.

entries.storyHtml: Suntosa is a small ~10-room resort in a lane near the Na Ban pier — 8.5 from 120 reviews, from ฿2,000. What guests mention most is that it's a 2–3-minute walk from the pier to your room, with sea-view balconies and a warm, hands-on owner, and it currently ranks #1 among Koh Larn B&Bs/guesthouses on TripAdvisor. It suits travellers who want to stay near the pier on a budget with a sea view and skip the songthaew across the island. Honest notes from the reviews: it's a small place with no pool, the walls aren't great at blocking sound, the entrance is a narrow sandy lane, the island is quiet at night, and prices rise on long weekends.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Take a Superior Room with Sea View for a sea-view balcony — better value than a standard room. Prices climb on long weekends so book ahead, and since the entrance is a sandy lane, a backpack rolls easier than a wheeled case.

entries.storyHtml: Koh Larn White House is a budget guesthouse in Na Ban village with a lot of reviews — 256 — scoring 8.0, from ฿1,200. What guests mention most is small but clean rooms with cold air-con, a walk from the Na Ban pier, and shops and the community market nearby. It suits travellers doing Koh Larn cheaply who weight price and cleanliness first, out at the beaches all day and back just to sleep, for low four figures. Honest notes from the reviews: rooms and bathrooms are small, there's no pool and no sea view, and breakfast is simple.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, take the Deluxe Double With Balcony for a spot to sit out. There's no pool and no sea view here, so if you want beachfront choose elsewhere on this list — and walk out for food in the nearby Na Ban village.

entries.storyHtml: Koh Larn Sea Side Resort is a small 15-room seaside resort with the lowest starting price in this guide — from just ฿900, scoring 8.0. What guests mention most is that it's about 300 metres from the Na Ban pier, every room is an air-con room with a balcony, and there's a seaside seating area for evening views. Reviews praise the owner/staff who run it themselves and often upgrade you to a sea-view room at a good price. It suits travellers who want a seaside stay on a budget close to the pier. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool, no full breakfast (free tea, coffee and toast are provided), rooms are simple, and it's not on a sandy beach you walk straight into.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Step up to the ฿1,200 Sea View Room for a sea-facing balcony — better value than the garden-view room. There's no full breakfast, so plan to grab food in the nearby Na Ban village, and message the owner about a pier pickup.

faqTitle: FAQ — common questions about value & budget stays on Koh Larn

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best value / budget stay on Koh Larn?
faq.a: It depends on your trip · For overall value, Toonja Koh Larn has the highest score in the set at 9.2, from ฿1,100 — a seaside stay ~3-min walk from the pier with a free golf-cart pickup · For the lowest starting price, Koh Larn Sea Side Resort from ฿900 is the cheapest · To sleep by the beach, Tawaen Beach Resort (Tawaen) and Xanadu Beach Resort (Samae Beach) · To save on getting around, Kampu Resort comes with a free scooter and pier shuttle

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays on Koh Larn cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start from around ฿900–2,450 a night · The lightest is Koh Larn Sea Side Resort from ฿900 · Low four figures are Toonja ฿1,100, The Castello and Koh Larn White House ฿1,200 · Mid-range are Kampu ฿1,600, Rimtalay and Tawaen ฿1,800, Xanadu ฿1,900 · A little higher are Suntosa ฿2,000 and Lareena ฿2,450 · Island prices run higher than Pattaya and rise on long weekends

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Koh Larn stays are on or near the beach?
faq.a: In this set, Tawaen Beach Resort sits on Tawaen Beach, about 150 m from the sea, an easy walk down to swim · Xanadu Beach Resort is right on Samae Beach with a free private beach and loungers · The Castello is near Tawaen Beach with a free shuttle to the sand · The Na Ban village stays (Kampu, White House, Sea Side, Suntosa, Lareena) aren't on a sandy beach — you take a songthaew or scooter to swim

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Larn and to your hotel?
faq.a: From Pattaya you take a ferry from Bali Hai pier to Na Ban pier or Tawaen pier (the regular ferry takes about 45 minutes; speedboats are faster but pricier) · Private cars can't go over — on the island you use shared songthaews, a rented scooter (around ฿300/day), or your hotel's shuttle · Stays around the Na Ban pier (Toonja, Suntosa, Lareena, Sea Side, White House, Kampu) are a walk from the boat, while beach stays (Tawaen, Xanadu) take a songthaew or the hotel shuttle

faq.q: ❓ Which Koh Larn stays are a walk from the pier, with no transfer needed?
faq.a: Several here are a walk from the Na Ban pier · Toonja ~3 min, with a free golf-cart pickup · Suntosa 2–3 min · Koh Larn Sea Side about 300 m · Lareena right by the pier, walk from the boat to your room · Kampu and White House are in Na Ban village, a walk from the pier · Ideal if you'd rather not drag bags onto a songthaew across the island

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book, and what should you prepare?
faq.a: Most good-value island stays are small (some just ~10–15 rooms), so they fill fast · On long weekends and in high season, book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, and prices rise · What to prepare: cash, since many shops and stays prefer it over cards and island ATMs are limited · Budget for a songthaew or a scooter rental around ฿300/day to get around · Check the return ferry times to Pattaya in advance · Most platforms offer Free Cancellation — lock a rate like that first, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
